it would be nice to have a fix landing in a hotfix release as this is quite an annoying regression

Confirmed on `v4.5.stable.official [876b29033]` and `v4.6.dev.custom_build [06827c91c]` but not `v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6]` when using Wayland. Also occurs with the main Run button, not just Run Current Scene. Also occurs on `v4.6.dev.custom_build [06827c91c]` when using X11.

```
Godot v4.6.dev (06827c91c) - Pop!_OS 22.04 LTS on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (nvidia; 575.64.05) - AMD Ryzen 7 3700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.28 GiB memory
```

```
Godot v4.6.dev (06827c91c) - Pop!_OS 22.04 LTS on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (nvidia; 575.64.05) - AMD Ryzen 7 3700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.28 GiB memory
```
cc. @deralmas

Hi! I can't replicate this issue, not even with the project you attached (which is an empty project), but I think I have an idea of what's going on.

I've finally just pinpointed the reason behind a very annoying completely random stall that would happen at initialization, where the Wayland event loop would randomly block forever. It caused lots of pain with the [embedder PR](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/107435) and the symptoms sound very similar.

Could you please tell me if #111493 solves your issue?

That said, the fact that this also happens on the X11 driver is mildly concerning but might be something different.

@CreatedBySeb to be completely clear, you've been using the X11 *display driver* in both cases. The only thing that changes is the environment. Wayland compositors have a compatibility system called XWayland, which allows them to run X11 apps natively. To try the Wayland backend, you have [to opt in](https://godotengine.org/article/dev-snapshot-godot-4-3-dev-3/#wayland-support-for-linux) as it's considered experimental and still misses some features, like game embedding.
I am experiencing this issue on Zorin 17. Have reverted back to 4.4.
Hi @LexGear, could you please try #111493 and see if that solves your issue?
i tried it and it doesn't fix it

That's weird. I'm not aware of other issues like that. I can't replicate this on sway 1.11, kernel 6.16.0+ (asus wmi patch), on a RADV RENOIR AMD iGPU, even without the race condition fix.

Could you please take a full debug log and send me the result?

```
WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 path/to/godot --verbose 2>&1 | tee debug.log
```

As usual, please note that this dump will also include any input sent to the editor.

[debug.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22926561/debug.log)
as additional information, i'm on hyprland, kernel 6.17.1
maybe hyprland implements things differently and it leads to this issue?

@enderprism I don't see anything off, when it comes to running the game :/

Maybe it's crashing, somehow? Does `dmesg` tell you about any segfault after replicating this issue? (You might have to run it as the superuser)

>  maybe hyprland implements things differently and it leads to this issue?

I don't think so, note that the "separate window" mode is literally just running the game with the arguments written in the logs, it's not doing anything fancier than that and should definitely not be compositor specific.

I can see that there are two "Running" entries, one working normally and another just... Doing nothing? A similar thing happened with that stall the above PR fixes, but even then it would print at least _something_.

Maybe it's some obscure graphics driver thing? Does this happen with GLES3?

GLES3 works fine (it works on the Compatibility backend)
must be a Vulkan + NVidia issue then?

Dunno, perhaps. The weird thing is that the logs don't include any vulkan error. Maybe hyprland is indeed doing something funky? Could you try some other compositor?

Can anybody replicate this on vulkan + other vendors?

> GLES3 works fine (it works on the Compatibility backend) must be a Vulkan + NVidia issue then?
